chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Dāwūd al-Ṣarmī, who said:
One day I was with Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام. He sat speaking until the sun had set, then he called for a candle while he remained seated speaking.
When I went out of the house, I looked and the twilight had disappeared before he performed the maghrib prayer. Then he called for water, performed wudu (ablution), and prayed.

So the first way of understanding these reports is one of two things: one of them is that he only instructed them to delay maghrib a little and to observe precaution so that by that they would be certain of the setting of the sun, because its criterion is the disappearance of the redness from the eastern side, not its disappearance from sight. This indicates that.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: the twilight glow whose disappearance is used as a sign
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةِ: the redness in the eastern sky that must disappear
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the eastern direction, where the redness is observed
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib prayer, whose beginning time is being discussed
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةُ: the disappearance or setting that marks the legal threshold
key_terms.يَحْتَاطُوا: to act with precaution in determining the proper time

ai.seo_question: When does the time of maghrib begin according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report describes the timing of maghrib prayer in relation to the disappearance of twilight. It indicates that the legal criterion is not merely the sun's vanishing from view, but the disappearance of the eastern redness, reflecting precaution in determining the prayer time.
